package_info.package_manager: N/A (injected JavaScript via third-party services or direct site compromise)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects any version of compromised scripts or sites)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire injected JavaScript package is malicious because it is designed to covertly capture sensitive payment and personal information from e-commerce website users during checkout and exfiltrate this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure without user or merchant consent. This behavior directly facilitates large-scale theft of payment credentials and personal data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, specifically when a user submits a payment or checkout form
execution_context.file_location: Injected into e-commerce site pages or within third-party JavaScript libraries (such as advertising, live chat, or customer rating scripts) loaded on checkout/payment pages
required_permissions: Access to the DOM (to read form fields)
Possibly access to local storage or cookies (if extended to capture session data)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the payment form, the code attaches an event listener to the form's submit event, programmatically collects sensitive payment and personal data from specific input fields, and transmits this data via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in the exfiltration of payment credentials and personal information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts payment form submissions and exfiltrates sensitive data (such as card number, expiration date, and CVV) to an external, hardcoded domain not associated with the merchant or any legitimate payment processor. This is a classic indicator of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment gateways or the merchant's own backend infrastructure, never to unknown or undocumented third-party domains. The presence of code that collects sensitive fields and sends them to an untrusted endpoint is a direct violation of secure payment processing practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may collect form data for submission to payment processors or for analytics, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and never to hardcoded, unrecognized domains. Additionally, legitimate analytics scripts do not collect full payment credentials.
key_indicators: JavaScript event listeners attached to payment or checkout form submission events
Programmatic access to sensitive input fields (e.g., card number, CVV, expiration date, name)
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded, untrusted, or previously unseen external domains during checkout
Presence of network request logic (e.g., XMLHttpRequest or fetch) within scripts loaded on payment pages
Scripts injected into or modifying third-party libraries not intended for payment processing

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the e-commerce site or a third-party JavaScript provider by exploiting a vulnerability, using stolen credentials, or through social engineering.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript injection into site or third-party script

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the website's codebase or a third-party script that is loaded by multiple e-commerce sites, ensuring widespread distribution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in the browsers of site visitors

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits payment information during checkout, the malicious code executes, capturing form data and exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data from compromised users

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or checkout form submission events
Client-side scripts that programmatically access and read sensitive payment fields (e.g., credit card number, CVV, expiration date, cardholder name)
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from client-side code to hardcoded or previously unseen external domains during the checkout process
Presence of network request logic (such as XMLHttpRequest or fetch) within scripts loaded on payment or checkout pages
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or additions to third-party JavaScript libraries (such as advertising, chat, or rating scripts) loaded on checkout pages
New or modified inline scripts present on payment or checkout pages that were not part of the original site deployment
Obfuscated or minified code containing network request logic or references to external domains within scripts on sensitive pages
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains or IP addresses not associated with the merchant, payment processor, or known service providers, especially during checkout
Frequent small POST requests from client browsers to external domains during the payment process
Outbound connections to hardcoded domains (e.g., https://attacker.com/collect) from payment or checkout pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unauthorized or unexpected JavaScript changes on payment and checkout pages, focusing on scripts that access sensitive form fields and initiate outbound network requests. Implement file integrity monitoring on all web assets, including third-party scripts, and scan for new or modified inline scripts. Analyze client-side network traffic for suspicious POST requests to unknown or untrusted domains during checkout. Employ vulnerability scanning and penetration testing to identify and remediate points of JavaScript injection. Maintain an allowlist of trusted domains for payment data transmission and alert on any deviations.
